title: "Tea, Caffeine & Decision Companion"
---

## Story in one minute

Imagine you pour hot water over tea leaves. Color and smell change. Later you feel a bit more awake, maybe a bit calmer. This site explains **why that happens**, using facts checked against owner-supplied source packs—not marketing slogans.

You do not need chemistry or psychology class. If a smart high-school student can follow a clear explanation with an everyday example, you are in the right place.

## Who this is for

This guide is for **curious beginners**: high-school and early college readers who want plain English. The owner of this site is an economist. We do **not** invent economic theories here. We only explain tea chemistry, how a cup can relate to alertness and calm, how tea shaped trade and ritual, and how researchers study drinks and decisions—using numbers and stories already in the source packs.

## What you will learn (four modules)

Think of the site as four rooms in one house. You can visit any room first.

1. **[The Chemical Core](modules/module-01.qmd)** — Tea comes from one plant species with two main types. How the leaf is processed (green vs black) and how you brew it changes what ends up in your cup.
2. **[Body, Brain & Mood](modules/module-02.qmd)** — Caffeine wakes you up by blocking a “time for sleep” signal. L-theanine (a calming amino acid in tea) tends to support calm focus. Researchers measure this with brain-wave patterns, stress hormones, and simple body signals—not only with how you feel.
3. **[History, Ritual & Warmth](modules/module-03.qmd)** — Tea remade trade balances, became a monastic focus aid, and—even as a warm mug in the hand—shows up in psychology experiments on trust. A short brewing break can also act as a practical stress reset.
4. **[Decisions & Choices](modules/module-04.qmd)** — Drinks do not flip a magic “smart switch.” They can nudge how fast you answer, how much risk you take, how much you care about tomorrow, and how trusting you are in a first move. Lab games measure those nudges.

## How to use this site

- Start with any module, or skim the [Modules overview](modules/index.qmd).
- When a number appears (for example “about 30–50 mg caffeine”), treat it as a **typical range from the packs**, not a promise about your exact mug.
- When a technical word appears, we define it in plain language the first time. You can also check the [Glossary](glossary.qmd).
- [Linkages](linkages.qmd) shows how ideas across modules connect (for example: brew temperature → what ends up in the cup → how you might feel later).
- [Cup reference](cup-reference.qmd) is a quick table of what is often in a 250 mL cup.
- [Bibliography](bibliography.qmd) lists the sources. We keep a few useful numbers on the pages; dense lab detail stays in the papers.

## What we deliberately leave out

We do **not** invent new percentages, mechanisms, history figures, or study results. We do **not** paste walls of lab equations. Everything here should trace back to the verified packs or the bibliography list.
